title: CascadePay — account playbook (scratch)
content:
Goal: land a POC with CascadePay (mid-market payments processor, ~250 employees). Primary objective: prove 50% token-cost reduction vs their current vanilla hosted LLM + maintain <200ms p95 latency for customer-facing flows. Secondary: show Dedicated or Private as path for regulated customers.

Quick account summary (notes/claims to confirm):
- HQ: Denver. Founded 2016. Focus: merchant payouts, instant-settlement rails for SMBs.
- ARR est: $30–60M (public hiring + funding signals).
- Tech: services on AWS (EKS), Postgres (Aurora), Kafka. They run some models inference via managed endpoints (company engineering blog mentions OpenAI + repurposed transformer clusters).
- Security posture: SOC2 type II claimed, PCI-compliant handling of card data, sensitive to customer PII leakage.
- Decision makers (hypothesis):
  - Head of ML / Director ML Ops — "Aisha Patel" (likely champion)
  - CTO — "Marco Ruiz" (economic + platform decisions)
  - Head of Product — "Nora Liang" (use‑cases: dispute automation, fraud)
  - Security/compliance review — "Infosec: Jacob Meyers"

Why Redwood matters for them (quick value props to use in outreach):
- Predictable unit economics: suggested batching + quantization -> big token cost wins for high throughput embeddings + chat.
- Private & Dedicated options for PCI/PII isolation (so legal/security checkbox).
- Smart routing & fallbacks reduce outage risk vs single vendor endpoints.
- Observability: token-level cost visibility + rollout control (useful for risk-managed rollouts across merchants).

Top candidate use-cases to pitch (order for POC):
1) Customer support chat assistant + note-summarization on support tickets (low-risk, quick win).
   - Metric: reduce avg handle time by 20%, latency p95 < 200ms for agent-facing completions.
2) Real-time fraud-reranking for high-value payouts (higher-risk, but high ROI).
   - Metric: improve precision at top-K by X% (we need baseline from Aisha).
3) Embedded merchant insights (search/semantic similarity over receipts) — cost-sensitive (embeddings).
   - Metric: cost per 1M embeddings tokens, compare quantization/vs current.

Outbound touch plan (sequence, short):
- Day 0: LinkedIn intro to Aisha (short, refer to common thread: AWS + fraud focus). Message A: "Aisha — saw your post on model infra cost at ScaleConf; small idea for reducing inference spend while keeping latency — would love 15 mins to share numbers."
- Day 3: Email to Aisha (formal), CC product eng alias if found. Email draft below.
- Day 7: Call+voicemail to office line (ask for intro to Nora for product use-cases).
- Day 14: Breakout note to Marco (CTO) with one-pager: 3-slide POC plan + success metrics + security anchor.

Email draft (short, for Day 3):
Subject: Cut inference cost for real-time support + fraud at CascadePay (15m)
Hi Aisha,

I’m Maya — account lead at Redwood Inference. We help payments companies keep real-time LLM features (chat, rerank, embeddings) fast and 3x–5x cheaper in production by combining batching, KV caching, and deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private).

Quick thought: for a high-volume support/rerank flow we recently ran a small POC that reduced token costs ~48% versus an unconstrained hosted endpoint while keeping p95 latency under 150ms. Happy to share the short POC plan and metrics — 15 minutes this week?

If not you, could you point me to the person owning model infra or fraud scoring?

Thanks,
Maya Chen
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

LinkedIn touch ideas: keep it 1–2 lines, mention ScaleConf or data infra talk.

Cold call script bullets (30–60s):
- Hook: "Maya from Redwood — we shave inference spend and keep p95 latency low for payments teams."
- Quick qualifier: "Are you running any production LLMs today for support/fraud?"
- Value: "We did a POC with a payments company that cut token spend ~50% while meeting latency SLOs via batching + private routing."
- Ask: "15 minutes to walk through a 2-week POC plan?"

Objections + suggested responses (cheat sheet):
- "We use OpenAI and don't want another vendor":
  - Response: "Totally — Redwood can sit in front of hosted endpoints as a broker first (no migration), then show cost/latency delta. Private/Dedicated is optional later for isolation."
- "We're worried about PCI / PII":
  - Response: "We offer Private deployment with customer-managed VPC and KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs for compliance. Happy to loop legal/security for a quick checklist review."
- "Latency is non-negotiable":
  - Response: "We can start with a narrow agent-facing route (higher latency budget) and gradually expand. Our runtime's continuous batching and KV cache typically improves p95 for repeat contexts."
- "We don't have bandwidth":
  - Response: "POC is turnkey: 2-week plan, we provide a sample workload harness + dev-support (SE). Low engineering touch required — will scope to your existing infra (AWS/EKS)."

POC proposal (2-week, lightweight):
- Week 0 (prep): sign NDA + access review (security), share small dataset (support transcripts / fraud signals).
- Week 1: adapter + baseline run (compare current endpoint profile: latency, cost, token counts). Redwood runs same prompts, measures costs, proposes batching/quantization profile.
- Week 2: tuned run + dashboard access (Console views: token-level cost, per-route latency). Final readout with clear cost delta + latency graphs.

Key success metrics to include in POC doc:
- Cost reduction (%) on token spend for target flow
- Latency p95 (ms) for the same flow
- Throughput (rps) at assessed provisioning
- Accuracy/regression checks (basic evals on prompt set)

Engineering notes / potential blockers:
- Need sample traffic shape: distribution of prompt lengths, concurrency, peak windows. Ask Aisha for 7-day trace export.
- Check whether current infra uses ephemeral keys to OpenAI or a shared org key — affects onboarding.
- If they enforce strict egress restrictions, Private deployment may be necessary (longer timeline).

Internal ask for SEs:
- Liam: can you sketch a one-pager with: cost model comparison (1M tokens baseline), proposed batching params (batch size, latency tradeoff), and suggested quantization level for their LLM family?
- Sana: security checklist + quick note on KMS/HSM integrations we would need for their PCI environment.

Open questions to resolve before call:
- Which models are in heavy use today (GPT variants, local models)?
- What is their peak concurrent requests and avg tokens/request?
- Do they use streaming responses for agent tooling?
- Legal: any restrictions on storing transcriptions/embeddings?

Notes for follow-up one-pager: include concrete numbers: cost per 1M tokens (hosted baseline), projected cost on Redwood hosted with batching, and Dedicated reserved pricing ballpark. Use the call to calibrate exact numbers.

Next steps (my personal checklist):
- [ ] Send LinkedIn note to Aisha (today).
- [ ] Email draft to Aisha + cc product eng alias (tomorrow).
- [ ] Create POC one-pager (Liam) + security checklist (Sana) by EOD Fri.
- [ ] If no reply in 7 days, reach out to Nora (product) and Marco (CTO) with brief deck.

Scratchpad thoughts / improv snippets to use in outreach:
- "Reduce inference spend without sacrificing latency"
- "Keep merchant data in your VPC — meet PCI controls"
- "2-week POC: no heavy infra changes, we adapter to existing endpoints"

Last-minute: look for recent hiring signals (fraud team) on LinkedIn — that signals urgency. Also check blog for "scale" posts mentioning LLM usage.

---
Raw: do not share externally: rough notes on negotiation points if they ask for lower pricing in exchange for commitment: offer 6–12 month reserved Dedicated discount, include uplift for support SLA.

End of doc.
